title: Bench test of the arimoclomol–Pompe hypothesis

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding: its weakest link is the claim that protein destabilization or misfolding drives GAA-related disorders (Pompe disease).
Test whether arimoclomol improves a protein destabilization or misfolding readout in a Pompe cell model.
Before starting, identify a suitable cell model and readout; the supplied asset list names no existing model or assay, so these would need to be sourced or built.
Ask whether the same readout used in the therapy’s known disease setting can be adopted, rather than assuming an assay is already available.
Compare the selected destabilization or misfolding readout with and without arimoclomol.
Consider GAA stabilization and cellular GAA levels as candidate measurements: the cited chaperone work reports stabilization of GAA and potentially higher cellular GAA levels.
Use the same model without arimoclomol as the comparison, keeping the readout and experimental conditions matched.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Rescue of the selected readout would justify further bench validation; no effect would retire this link from the current plan.
Arimoclomol’s proposed mechanism is contested, and its clinical mechanism in NPC is unknown.
The shared mechanism is not disease-specific, symptom overlap with NPC is minimal, and the graph contains no study testing this therapy class in Pompe disease.
